intentRefinerTrial.originalIntent: PRISM is BIG's mobile-first Copilot and GO Hub client. SPECTRUM should let BIG access and coordinate GO Hub from one surface, use GO/LIGHT without app-switching, keep Ledger as finance owner, Map as the main map surface with Ride optional, remove the appointment-calendar surface, retain Browser/Observer, and use a Device Bridge as BIG's bounded on-device fingers.

challenges: If SPECTRUM owns every domain rule it becomes another bloated Lighthouse.
One Copilot surface can hide provenance if capability ownership is not explicit.
newKnowledge: Introduce a Capability Registry/Manifest: capability owner, source of truth, read/write contract, authority requirement, adapter, verification method.
Use a Context Broker so Copilot receives only the relevant working set instead of dumping all GO Hub state into the model.

challenges: Using screen typing as the message transport risks duplicate sends, context drift, and UI breakage.
GO↔LIGHT relay can become an infinite conversational loop.
newKnowledge: Counter/GO Hub remains the canonical handoff transcript; Device Bridge is only a wake/delivery layer.
Every device action needs an idempotent signed dispatch envelope with counterId/workId/checkpointId/target/action/expectedUi/timeout.
GO↔LIGHT conference must be objective-bound and terminate on ANSWERED/BLOCKED/NEED_BIG/DONE/MAX_TURNS/TIMEOUT.

challenges: PRISM concentrates device control, GO Hub access, and financial data in one app.
BIG has no computer, so a bad mobile update could remove the only control surface.
newKnowledge: Ledger needs a separate encrypted financial vault and prompt-minimization boundary; Copilot gets scoped summaries, not raw finance by default.
Secrets/tokens stay outside model context and use device-backed secure storage where available.
Migration needs a recovery/rollback path independent of the new PRISM shell; preserve Lighthouse legacy aliases until device verification succeeds.
Cloud build artifacts need provenance/hash verification before device install.

challenges: Auto-refining every tiny command could make PRISM slow and annoying.
A single Copilot surface could become opaque if work state is hidden.
newKnowledge: Intent Refiner depth should be saturation-driven: trivial intent can saturate in one pass; project-level/ambiguous intent continues.
Expose inline route/authority/receipt evidence in Copilot instead of forcing BIG into dashboards.
Calendar surface is removed from PRISM; do not silently delete the underlying Hub calendar capability unless BIG explicitly asks.

challenges: GO Hub offline or route unresolved.
newKnowledge: Fail closed on unresolved Work/Route/Authority; queue locally rather than inventing truth.
Never create a new Work from similarity alone.
Device Bridge must verify before/after actuation and dedupe by dispatch id.
Missing receipt remains WAIT/UNKNOWN, never DONE.

challenges: Search for a new material contradiction across architecture, authority, handoff, security, recovery and UX.

workingIntent.definition: A mobile-first owner cockpit where BIG uses one Copilot surface while SPECTRUM orchestrates governed GO Hub capabilities without owning their domain truth.
workingIntent.agentCoordination: Counter is canonical; device typing only wakes/routes the correct agent.
workingIntent.finance: Ledger owns finance data behind a separate protected boundary; Copilot receives scoped finance context.
workingIntent.device: API/Hub first, then deeplink/intent, Accessibility+IME only as verified last-mile actuation.
workingIntent.resilience: Cloud does heavy work; mobile remains recoverable with verified build provenance and rollback/legacy path.
workingIntent.authority: BIG remains owner; PRISM coordinates but never self-approves owner-only actions.

unknowns: Actual Android Device Bridge behavior against the target chat app has not been exercised.
A live inventory of every GO Hub capability/adapter still needs to be mapped into the Capability Registry.
PRISM migration/build/install/rollback from LIGHTHOUSE PR #178 has not been device-tested.

decisionRules.rule: Resolve an existing Work/Checkpoint before creating or dispatching anything.
Represent missing, ambiguous, or stale evidence as UNKNOWN; never infer a positive fact.
If Work, Route, Authority, or requested change is unresolved, ASK or WAIT and do not dispatch.
Refinement may clarify intent but cannot rewrite owner intent or expand authority.
Derive an idempotency key from Work, Checkpoint, action type, and normalized target; check existing receipt before dispatch.
COMPLETE requires receipt plus readback/evidence from the responsible owner.
GO/LIGHT handoff uses the same Work/Checkpoint and bounded relay; Counter remains canonical transcript.

actions.read: Allowed when source and scope are known; return source references.
actions.plan: Allowed without mutation; produce route, authority, risks, and next step.
actions.ask: Required when ambiguity materially changes the action.
actions.dispatch: Only when Work, Route, Authority, idempotency, and confirmation gates pass.
actions.verify: Read owner truth and evidence; never trust model self-report.
actions.return: Return result on the same Work/Checkpoint.

routePolicy.lighthouse: Only explicit integration intent with separate capability and receipt
routePolicy.deviceBridge: Last-mile actuation only when capability is verified
routePolicy.manual: Fail closed; surface owner action required

privacy: minimize prompt data sent to Ledger
do not retain passwords or raw private input

assistantRole.mission: Act as BIG's personal AI assistant across the Shop and Office clients, coordinating shared context and governed work through GO Hub.
does: understand BIG's request from either Shop or Office
maintain one governed Work/Checkpoint context across both clients
coordinate shared data reads and handoffs through GO Hub

salesSet.name: Hero
salesSet.goal: Stop the viewer. Normal place, one wrong-era detail.

salesSet.name: Before
salesSet.goal: Establish the same location as completely usable and ordinary.

salesSet.name: First Clue
salesSet.goal: Reveal a short old stone staircase where modern solid ground should be.

salesSet.name: Old Access
salesSet.goal: Open the same stone doorway into an older corridor belonging to the same building.

salesSet.name: Functional Mismatch
salesSet.goal: Show modern infrastructure physically conflicting with the older layout.

salesSet.name: Product Proof
salesSet.goal: Keep a clean illuminated insert area for a real template screenshot added later; generate no device or UI.

promptSet.master: Grounded cinematic editorial illustration, photorealistic believable architecture, ordinary canal-side urban service district at warm dusk, restrained color palette, eye-level camera, medium framing, same narrow canal, same small stone bridge, same occupied main building, same old stone arch doorway, same modern pedestrian/transit infrastructure. The location is functional and lived-in, not picturesque. Keep 80% ordinary present-day reality and only 20% anomaly. No text, labels, logos, UI, watermarks, portals, cosmic effects, giant skyline, apocalypse, or clutter.

images.name: Hero
images.prompt: Show the ordinary district in use. The old stone arch doorway is visually clear but believable; introduce exactly one subtle wrong-era detail near it, such as a few old stone steps interrupting the modern pavement. Leave calm negative space for title added later. No sightseeing panorama.

images.name: Before
images.prompt: Show the exact same camera family and recurring anchors before anything is obviously wrong. Canal, bridge, main building, arch doorway, pavement and transit elements all function normally. Quiet everyday realism; the doorway reads as old but not mysterious.

images.name: First Clue
images.prompt: Same place and anchors. A short weathered stone staircase now emerges where the modern street plan should be solid ground. Make the contradiction physically clear but modest enough that a passerby might rationalize it. Everything else stays normal.

images.name: Old Access
images.prompt: Same stone arch doorway, now open. Behind it is a physically continuous older corridor inside the same building footprint: stone floor, old masonry, believable depth and construction. It must not resemble a portal or another dimension.

images.name: Functional Mismatch
images.prompt: Same district. Show one clear infrastructure consequence: a modern transit/service corridor follows its normal path but terminates at an older masonry wall or old passage alignment, forcing two incompatible routes through the same physical location. No explosion, collapse, or spectacle.

images.name: Product Proof
images.prompt: Use the same visual identity but simplify the scene heavily. Provide a clean, well-lit editorial composition with a large empty rectangular insert area intended for a real Notion template screenshot added later. Do not generate a laptop, phone, browser window, fake interface, fake writing, or placeholder text.

presentationRule.rule: Choose exactly one point to present. Every visible element must support that point.
presentationRule.emphasis: The point does not need to be exaggerated, but the viewer must recognize what the image is about immediately.
hierarchy: Supporting elements: push attention toward the point
presentationRule.rejectionTest: If a viewer first notices the scenery, mood, city, or decoration instead of the intended point, the image fails.

visualRenderPackets.intent: Design FORGE LAB as a tangible, high-function engineering workbench where BIG can understand the active build by looking at one central artifact, not by reading a dashboard.
visualRenderPackets.requestedResult: A first visual concept for the FORGE LAB interface that feels like a compact precision workshop: central Forge Bench, pinned Mission/Build Recipe above, materials feeding in from the left, evidence/testing on the right, version/evidence track below, and one deliberate Factory Dock exit.
mustKeep: Mission Clamp and Build Recipe above the bench
Material Rack feeds the bench from the left
Factory Dock visually separate from edit controls
One Work Card / one primary artifact focus
mustRemove: merge/deploy buttons mixed into normal editing
constraints: Desktop-like workbench composition even if later adapted to mobile
Use physical metaphors—tray, clamp, rack, bench, dock—rather than floating dashboard cards
Central artifact must be readable within one glance
State colors only for evidence/status, not decoration
Blocked state should dim unrelated areas and pin the exact blocker near the artifact
Ready-for-Factory state may reveal/activate the Factory Dock but must not imply automatic authority
unknowns: Exact visual language of FORGE LAB has not yet been rendered; spacing and hierarchy must be verified from the first image.
First render must verify whether the left/right rails feel like real workspace furniture rather than dashboard panels.
Exact responsive behavior on PRISM/mobile is intentionally out of scope for this first Forge Lab visual.
